To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the optimal state references for PMSM drives can be computed using a constrained MTPA optimization problem, that the maximum and intersection problems can be solved to compute the optimal state references, and that a procedure is proposed to compute locally optimized PMSM parameters that take magnetic saturation into account.
the proposed method provides a torque controller for PMSM drives with a minimum of hardware components and that the proposed algorithm is sufficiently efficient for implementation in real time.
we propose a procedure to map a torque request onto optimal current reference that minimizes conduction and switching loss.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the optimal computation of state (currents) references for a PMSM.
the design and implementation of a torque controller for PM machines that optimizes the efficiency at any speed.
the optimal control of permanent magnet machines.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a novel optimal state reference computation algorithm is proposed that is compatible with a wide range of state (current), machine, control and power converter topologies.
the proposed approach is a significant advance over the state of the art, and is expected to have a significant impact on PMSM drive design and operation.
this research provides a procedure to compute optimal state references for a PMSM drive.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed procedure provides optimal state references for a given PMSM torque and dc link voltage.
the proposed method is able to provide optimal current references that result in a high efficiency drive system.
a new torque control method is proposed that minimizes conduction and switching loss for a wide range of machine speeds and torque demands.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proposed procedure can be used to obtain high efficiency operation for any PMSM drive.
a torque controller that is optimized for efficiency can be implemented with the proposed procedure and dynamic (current) control.
the proposed torque controller can be implemented with any current controller, and it can be applied to any PMSM machine with/without PWM and with saliency.
